text: If $f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \int\limits _{0}^{x}(5+|1-t|)dt, & x>2 \\ 5x+1, & x\leq 2 \end{array} \right.$, then
options: f(x) is not continuous at x = 2
f(x) is continuous but not differentiable at x = 2
f(x) is not differentiable at x = 1
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\int\limits _{0}^{1}(5+(1-t))dt+\int\limits _{1}^{x}(5+(t-1))dt$

$=6-\frac{1}{2}+\left (4t+\frac{t^{2}}{2}\right )\left |_{1}^{x} \right.$

$=\frac{11}{2}+4x+\frac{x^{2}}{2}-4-\frac{1}{2}$

$=\frac{x^{2}}{2}+4x-1$

$f(2^{+})=2+8+1=11$

$f(2)=f(2^{-})=5\times 2+1=11$

$\Rightarrow$ continuous at x = 2

Clearly differentiable at x = 1

Lf' (2) = 5

Rf' (2) = 6

$\Rightarrow$ Not differentiable at x = 2
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

expansion of $\left (x\sin α+a\frac{\cos α}{x}\right )^{10}$ is $\frac{10!}{(5!)^{2}}$, then the value of 'a' is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$T_{r+1}={}^{10}C_{r}(x\sin α)^{10-r}\left (\frac{a\cos α}{x}\right )^{r}$

r = 0, 1, 2, ......., 10

$T_{r + 1}$ will be independent of x when 10 $-$ 2r = 0 $\Rightarrow$ r = 5

$T_{6}={}^{10}C_{5}(x\sin α)^{5}\times \left (\frac{a\cos α}{x}\right )^{5}$

$={}^{10}C_{5}\times a^{5}\times \frac{1}{2^{5}}(\sin 2α)^{5}$

will be greatest when sin2$α$ = 1

$\Rightarrow {}^{10}C_{5}\frac{a^{5}}{2^{5}}={}^{10}C_{5}\Rightarrow a=2$

text:
The lowest integer which is greater 

than $\left (1+\frac{1}{10^{100}}\right )^{10^{100}}$ is $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Let $P=\left (1+\frac{1}{10^{100}}\right )^{10^{100}}$

Let $x=10^{100}$

$\Rightarrow P=\left (1+\frac{1}{x}\right )^{x}$

$\Rightarrow P=1+(x)\left (\frac{1}{x}\right )+\frac{(x)(x-1)}{\left |2–}.\frac{1}{x^{2}}+\frac{(x)(x-1)(x-2)}{\right |3–}.\frac{1}{x^{3}}+....$

(upto $10^{100} + 1$ terms)

$\Rightarrow P=1+1+\left (\frac{1}{\left |2–}-\frac{1}{\right |2–x^{2}}\right )+\left (\frac{1}{\left |3–}-...\right )+... \right.$ so on

$\Rightarrow P=2+\left (Positivevaluelessthan\frac{1}{\left |2–}+\frac{1}{\right |3–}+\frac{1}{\left |4–}+...\right ) \right.$

Also $e=1+\frac{1}{\left |1–}+\frac{1}{\right |2–}+\frac{1}{\left |3–}+\frac{1}{\right |4–}+...$

$\Rightarrow \frac{1}{\left |2–}+\frac{1}{\right |3–}+\frac{1}{\left |4–}+...=e-2 \right.$

$\Rightarrow$ P = 2 + (positive value less than e $-$ 2)

$\Rightarrow$ P $\in$ (2, 3)

$\Rightarrow$ least integer value of P is 3
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text:
The number of distinct real roots 

of $\left |\begin{array}{lll} \sin x & \cos x & \cos x \\ \cos x & \sin x & \cos x \\ \cos x & \cos x & \sin x \end{array}\right |=0$ in the interval $-\frac{π}{4}\leq x\leq \frac{π}{4}$ is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left |\begin{array}{lll} \sin x & \cos x & \cos x \\ \cos x & \sin x & \cos x \\ \cos x & \cos x & \sin x \end{array}\right |=0,-\frac{π}{4}\leq x\leq \frac{π}{4}$

Apply : $R_{1}\to R_{1}-R_{2}$ & $R_{2}\to R_{2}-R_{3}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left |\begin{array}{lll} \sin x-\cos x & \cos x-\sin x & 0 \\ 0 & \sin x-\cos x & \cos x-\sin x \\ \cos x & \cos x & \sin x \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(\sin x-\cos x)^{2}\left |\begin{array}{lll} 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 \\ \cos x & \cos x & \sin x \end{array}\right |=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $(\sin x-\cos x)^{2}(\sin x+2\cos x)=0$

$\therefore$ $x=\frac{π}{4}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text:
Let y = y(x) be the solution of the differential 

equation xdy $= (y + x^{3}$ cosx)dx with y($π$) = 0, then $y\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )$ is equal to :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$xdy=(y+x^{3}\cos x)dx$

$\Rightarrow$ $xdy=ydx+x^{3}\cos xdx$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{xdy-ydx}{x^{2}}=\frac{x^{3}coxdx}{x^{2}}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{d}{dx}\left (\frac{y}{x}\right )=\int x\cos xdx$

$\Rightarrow \frac{y}{x}=x\sin x-\int 1.\sin xdx$

$\Rightarrow$ $\frac{y}{x}=x\sin x+\cos x+C$

$\Rightarrow 0=-1+C\Rightarrow C=1,x=π,y=0$

so, $\frac{y}{x}=x\sin x+\cos x+1$

$y=x^{2}\sin x+x\cos x+x$

$x=\frac{π}{2}$

$y\left (\frac{π}{2}\right )=\frac{π^{2}}{4}+\frac{π}{2}$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text:
Consider the function

where P(x) is a polynomial such that P'' (x) is always a constant and P(3) = 9. If f(x) is continuous at x = 2, then P(5) is equal to $_____________$.
[IMG]
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$f(x)=\left \{\begin{array}{ll} \frac{P(x)}{\sin (x-2)}, & x\neq 2 \\ 7, & x=2 \end{array} \right.$

P''(x) = const. $\Rightarrow$ P(x) is a 2 degree polynomial

f(x) is cont. at x = 2

$f(2^{+}) = f(2^{-})$

$\lim _{x\to 2^{+}}\frac{P(x)}{\sin (x-2)}=7$

$\lim _{x\to 2^{+}}\frac{(x-2)(ax+b)}{\sin (x-2)}=7\Rightarrow 2a+b=7$

P(x) = (x $-$ 2)(ax + b)

P(3) = (3 $-$ 2)(3a + b) = 9 $\Rightarrow$ 3a + b = 9

a = 2, b = 3

P(5) = (5 $-$ 2)(2 $\times$ 5 + 3) = 3 $\times$ 13 = 39
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: The equation of a circle is $Re(z^{2}) + 2(Im(z))^{2} + 2Re(z) = 0$, where z = x + iy. A line which passes through the center of the given circle and the vertex of the parabola, $x^{2}$ $-$ 6x $-$ y + 13 = 0, has y-intercept equal to $______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Equation of circle is $(x^{2}$ $-$ $y^{2}) + 2y^{2} + 2x = 0$

$x^{2} + y^{2} + 2x = 0$

Centre : ($-$1, 0)

Parabola : $x^{2}$ $-$ 6x $-$ y + 13 = 0

(x $-$ $3)^{2} = y$ $-$ 4

Vertex : (3, 4)

Equation of line $\equiv y-0=\frac{4-0}{3+1}(x+1)$

$y=x+1$

y-intercept = 1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift

text: If $\left (\vec{a}+3\vec{b}\right )$ is perpendicular to $\left (7\vec{a}-5\vec{b}\right )$ and $\left (\vec{a}-4\vec{b}\right )$ is perpendicular to $\left (7\vec{a}-2\vec{b}\right )$, then the angle between $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$ (in degrees) is $_______________$.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
$\left (\vec{a}+3\vec{b}\right )⊥\left (7\vec{a}-5\vec{b}\right )$

$\therefore$ $\left (\vec{a}+3\vec{b}\right ).\left (7\vec{a}-5\vec{b}\right )=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $7\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}-15\left |\vec{b}\right |^{2}+16\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ ....(1)

Also, $\left (\vec{a}-4\vec{b}\right ).\left (7\vec{a}-2\vec{b}\right )=0$

$\Rightarrow$ $7\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}+8\left |\vec{b}\right |^{2}-30\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ .....(2)

Equation (1) × 30

$210\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}-450\left |\vec{b}\right |^{2}+480\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ ....(3)

Equation (2) × 16

$112\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}+128\left |\vec{b}\right |^{2}-480\vec{a}.\vec{b}=0$ .....(4)

from (3) & (4)

$322\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}=322\left |\vec{b}\right |^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}=\left |\vec{b}\right |^{2}$

$\Rightarrow$ $\left |\vec{a}\right |=\left |\vec{b}\right |$

From equation (2),

$15\left |\vec{a}\right |=30\vec{a}.\vec{b}$

$\Rightarrow$ $15\left |\vec{a}\right |^{2}=30\left |\vec{a}\right |.\left |\vec{b}\right |\cos θ$

$\cos θ=\frac{15}{30}=\frac{1}{2}$

$\therefore$ $θ=60^{\circ }$
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2021 (Online) 25th July Evening Shift
